summary: Correct, well-tested lesson on the classic 'editing a record makes it look like its own duplicate' bug: trim+lowercase key comparison with an item.id !== editingId exclusion, aria-invalid plus focus on rejection, and validation strictly before any mutation. Tests assert localStorage is byte-identical after a rejected create and a rejected edit. But it is ~8 lines of production code carrying 4,969 mostly-templated words, with no failed-write handling and no detection of pre-existing case-duplicates.

name: JS1/focus-timer
top_fix: Re-frame for CRUD transfer: add a 02-CONCEPTS subsection mapping the idempotency guard (app.js:117) onto a double-submitted POST / idempotency key, and remove the duplicated timer.mode = 'idle' at app.js:132 that the change introduced.
summary: Best-tested of the four plain-browser courses: deadline arithmetic replaces per-tick decrement, startTimer is idempotent, sub-second remainder survives pause, and a late callback cannot log a second session. The controllable-clock tests are precise (00:15 not 00:59 after a 45s stall; 58.75s remaining after a 1250ms pause; exactly one interval after a double start). Accuracy is perfect, but the domain is timers rather than CRUD — the only directly transferable idea is the idempotency guard — and the change left a duplicated mode assignment behind.

name: finance-dashboard

summary: The clearest update-a-record lesson in the browser half: editing reuses the entry modal in an explicit mode, forces the original id onto the replacement record, validates positive two-decimal amounts and real dates, and writes to storage before publishing so a quota failure leaves the original intact and the editor open. The failure test loops -1/0/1.001 and asserts the stored amount, then patches setItem to throw and checks state, modal state and error text. Six spot-checks passed including the line-791 excerpt. Undermined by the create path still mutating first, which the course glosses rather than teaches.

name: recipeweb
top_fix: Unpack the densest line in the change: add a step-by-step walkthrough of the ~200-character recipeSlugs expression in src/store/shoppingState.ts (is-array guard, type-predicate filter, membership check against recipes, Set dedupe) to 03-WORKED-CHANGE.md, with a bad input traced through each step.
summary: Best-verified course in the batch. normalizeShoppingState() is a hand-written runtime schema over localStorage — unknown/duplicate slugs, non-boolean checks, orphaned keys and >100-char overrides all dropped — plus an ingredientsWithQuantities() that keeps the screen and the clipboard reading the same effective values without mutating the source recipe. Four independent checks (tests, tsc+vite build, oxlint, Chromium) are all backed by checks.json, tsx is properly declared so npm install && npm test works clean, and all six spot-checks passed. Client-only, so no transactions or authz.

name: jobtrack
top_fix: Split the misleading count at astraupskill/VERIFICATION.md:12 — 'Automated test cases: 90' is the entire pre-existing 8-file Vitest suite, while Astra added 4 it-blocks in test/jobBackup.test.js. Report new cases and full-suite run separately, and warn that the suite takes ~8-10 minutes with one timeout-prone form test.
summary: Strongest code change in B01: a versioned daybook.jobs backup envelope whose validator enforces a 2MB/10,000-record cap, per-field bounds, non-blank id and company, in-set status, real YYYY-MM-DD dates, http/https-only URLs and duplicate-id rejection before a single storage write — and whose exporter re-parses its own output so it can never emit a file the importer rejects. Tests assert storage.set was not called on every rejection and toHaveBeenCalledExactlyOnceWith on success, and the module is genuinely wired into JobTracker.jsx's write queue. The 89/90 retry is disclosed honestly; the '90 test cases' headline is not.

name: newcodexJS/01-task-manager
top_fix: Fix 04-TESTING-AND-DEBUGGING.md: delete the jsdom/app.js paragraph at line 37 (wrong project) and the copy-pasted setup block at line 7 whose 'see chapter 4' pointer sits inside chapter 4; then add a Docker fallback (postgres:18 container + createdb astra_test_learning) since a local Postgres is the biggest drop-off point.
summary: The place to start for server-side CRUD testing. The production change is only five lines (int4-bounded ids so an oversized id is a 400 not a DB error, a 255-char title bound, and letting an overdue task be re-saved with its own past due date), but the new suite drives real HTTP through Express and reads rows back with Knex against a real PostgreSQL schema created and dropped per run, asserting completed_at flips across done/reopen and that rejected input leaves the row count unchanged. The harness refuses any database not named astra_test_*. VERIFICATION correctly omits a browser-check row, matching the evidence.

name: newcodexJS/02-contact-book
top_fix: Add an HTTP-level test for POST /api/contacts/import using harness.listen(app) as newcodexJS/01-task-manager does — the tests currently call service.importContacts() directly, so the controller, route wiring and 400-vs-500 status mapping for the headline feature are unverified.
summary: The densest and most transferable CRUD lesson in the batch: a real character-by-character CSV state machine (quoted commas, doubled quotes, embedded newlines, CRLF, BOM, and explicit rejection of ambiguous quoting), whole-batch validation before the transaction opens, one db.transaction covering contacts + tag upserts + junction rows, and an orderBy('contacts.id') tiebreaker that stops paginated lists repeating rows. Test 3 forces a late duplicate-email failure and proves even the orphan tag created midway is rolled back. All six spot-checks passed. Import writes row-by-row inside the transaction, which the course never mentions.

name: newcodexJS/03-expense-tracker
top_fix: Split the overloaded error at server/src/services/expenseService.js:14 — one message ('Amount must be greater than zero') is thrown for non-finite amounts, values above 99,999,999.99 and 1.001 alike — into four distinct messages and assert each string in test 3.
summary: A tight SQL lesson built on a genuine pre-existing bug: the category report inherited the row-level SELECT list, and the one-line .clearSelect() fix is used to teach why grouping changes what a row means. Validation now rejects impossible dates, bad months, reversed ranges and non-integer category ids before any SQL runs, and the hand-calculated leap-day fixture forces monthly, daily and category totals to reconcile to 3,500 cents while adjacent-month rows stay out. Honest about two unfixed warts — inclusive vs half-open ranges between endpoints, and a ::float cast on a decimal money column — but leaves both in the code.

name: newcodexJS/05-recipe-manager
top_fix: Add a second worked excerpt covering parseRecipeInput (recipeService.ts:17-63) — the densest new code in the project is never walked through — and change the default at recipeService.ts:55 from isPublic: body.isPublic !== false to === true, since an omitted field currently defaults to public in a course about private ownership.
summary: The capstone: authentication identifies the caller, authorization compares that caller with the stored owner, and ownership never comes from the request body — proved by a test where an authenticated Bob sends a forged user_id and still gets 403, alongside 401, 403-on-delete, 403-on-read and 200-for-owner. The ownership read moved inside the update transaction behind SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, the model update is scoped by user_id as a second barrier, and a validator that silently dropped blank ingredients now rejects them. The rollback test fails late on a foreign key so it proves atomicity, and all four claimed checks (tests, build, server+client typecheck) are backed by checks.json.
